title: Values computed by program gates
statement: Let $n,m,w$ be natural numbers, let the instruction kinds form a type with a designated default, and let $F$ assign a Boolean-list function to each kind. For an input assignment $x\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}^n$, a program of instructions whose source bits are valid for their instruction positions and whose source lists each have length $m$, and any $i\leq$ the program length, running the first $i$ stages of the constructed gate list on $x$ preserves every input bit, places false and true at vertices $n$ and $n+1$, respectively, and gives at each earlier instruction's output vertex the corresponding bit of that instruction's computed block.
hypotheses_covered: source bits of each instruction are valid for its position
each instruction's source list has length $m$
$i$ is at most the program length
